target_customer: Finance and accounting teams at mid-market and growth companies that run an ERP such as NetSuite, QuickBooks or Sage
problem: Accounts payable, accounts receivable, cash application and reconciliation still involve manual work done outside the accounting system, such as chasing customers for payment and matching invoices to purchase orders.
business_model: B2B SaaS, AI agent layer on top of the customer's existing ERP (pricing not published)
product_category: AI agents for finance and accounting operations

founders.name: Thomas Dowling
previous_startups: TaxProper (YC S19, acquired by Opendoor in 2022, per the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he advised the Mayor of Chicago and was appointed by the Illinois governor to oversee a state agency.

founders.name: Aaron Coppa
previous_startups: TaxProper (founding engineer, acquired by Opendoor in 2022)

competitors.name: Numeric
competitors.what: AI-powered month-end close and accounting automation software
competitors.funding_then: $10M seed (May 2024) and $28M Series A (Oct 2024); a later Series B appears only in one aggregator

competitors.name: FloQast
competitors.what: Established close management platform that markets itself against Numeric
competitors.traction_then: described as a fast growing startup in launch coverage

competitors.name: BlackLine
competitors.what: Incumbent financial close and accounting automation vendor
competitors.traction_then: established player named as the main incumbent

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents must log into many ERPs, billing and banking systems and match invoices to contracts reliably. The company claims SOC 2 Type 2, which signals real security work. The underlying LLM capability is available to everyone, so the hard part is integration and accuracy.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and workflow data give some switching costs, but several funded startups and incumbents sell similar AI close and AP/AR automation, and the model layer is shared.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of early 2026 incumbents and well funded startups already market AI agents for close and reconciliation; a Ramp comparison page promotes its own agent product. No acquisition of FullSeam found.

market_need_then: Finance teams spend heavy manual effort on AP, AR and reconciliation, and the AI accounting category drew many seed and Series A rounds in 2024 and 2025 (Numeric, Basis, Abacus and others appear in search results).

branding.domain_note: Uses fullseam.com, the exact name .com; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: Clean light layout with customer logos and comparison pages against FloQast, Numeric and BlackLine
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and plain spoken, for example Keep your ERP. Lose the manual work.

brand_strength.rationale: Early stage brand with no press about the brand itself found; the name is easily confused in search with Fullsteam and Fulshear results, and credibility comes mainly from the founders' prior exit.

outcome_analysis: FullSeam is an active Winter 2026 company, so no outcome exists yet. Its main strengths are a founding team that already sold a YC company to Opendoor and a clear wedge of AI agents sitting on top of existing ERPs. The risks are a crowded AI accounting category with funded rivals and incumbents, and no publicly verified funding to date.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators list a seed of about 500K from Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund and a seed dated 2026-03 with about 1M total, with no press release or company confirmation, so no round is recorded. A Caplight headline about a 16M Series A belongs to another company. The YC page names three founders, all from TaxProper. Search for outcome news found only unrelated Fullsteam results.
